subject: Next steps: Private endpoint readiness & egress model options

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: Private endpoint readiness & egress model options

Tom — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and clear next steps so your network/security team has what they need to evaluate a Private VPC deployment with Redwood.

Key notes from the call (high level):
- FinData preference: leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (cross-account architecture) for data residency + isolated networking.
- Remaining decisions: PrivateLink vs VPC peering, egress IP allowlist needs, TLS termination model, and cross-account routing approach.

Action items we need from you to proceed with a formal qualification:
1) Network inventory (subnets & CIDR) for the target VPC/accounts you plan to connect from — public and private subnets.
2) Preferred connection type: PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink endpoints) or VPC peering/cross-account peering. If unsure, tell us bandwidth and expected peak requests/min.
3) Egress policy: do you require a fixed set of outbound IPs (allowlist) for any callbacks to your systems or external services? If yes, please confirm that allowlist will be implemented on your firewall side and share the contact at networking/security.
4) TLS termination: will FinData terminate TLS at your ALB/NLB or do you want Redwood to present certs and handle TLS?
5) Maintenance windows and any blackout days for rollout/testing.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf (proposed timeline + responsibilities).

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- If you provide the network inventory and confirm the connection type, our infra team will produce a connection checklist (IPs, ports, SG/NACL rules) within 48 hours.
- If you need strict egress allowlist we recommend PrivateLink since it cleanly isolates traffic and eliminates the need for an outbound NAT on our side. For high-throughput workloads VPC peering is often simpler.

Can you share the network inventory spreadsheet and the security contact who will own the firewall allowlist? I can schedule a follow-up deep-dive with our infra lead (Rishi) tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Enterprise Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

Thanks, Ava — good summary. Per our internal notes from this morning: FinData is aiming for private connectivity and we prefer cross-account peering initially, but we are open to PrivateLink if the egress profile or security constraints demand it.

Answers to your questions:
- Network inventory: attached spreadsheet (fin_data_network_inventory.xlsx) includes account IDs, VPC IDs, and the subnet CIDR ranges we expect to use for the connector.
- Preferred connection: starting posture: VPC peering across accounts (we want direct routing for latency-sensitive inference). We may opt for PrivateLink if firewall constraints surface.
- Egress allowlist: we will require a deterministic set of Redwood outbound IPs for callbacks to our telemetry and metrics ingest endpoints. I don’t have the final list yet but platform-security@findata.com is the owner.
- TLS termination: FinData prefers to terminate TLS at our edge (ALB) and present mTLS to internal services. We’d like Redwood to support either option — we will share cert provisioning requirements if you can confirm support.
- Maintenance windows: standard window is Sat 0200–0600 PT; we can be flexible for initial testing.

I attached the inventory. Let me know what additional fields you need and we’ll loop in our network lead if helpful. Also — does Redwood provide egress IP ranges in a CIDR list (for firewall allowlist)?

Tom Hale
Director, Platform Security | FinData Analytics
tom.hale@findata.com

Hi Tom — copying Rishi infra notes into thread so we have a single technical record. Short answers + what we'll provide.

1) PrivateLink vs VPC peering (short):
- PrivateLink: best when the customer requires a tight outbound allowlist (we present service endpoints in your account and traffic never traverses public internet). Works well for strict firewall policies.
- VPC peering (cross-account): lower operational overhead for high-throughput workloads and simplified routing; however, you’ll need route distribution and careful NACL/SG control for inter-VPC traffic.

2) Redwood egress IPs / allowlist:
- We can publish a deterministic list of warm egress addresses for callbacks and webhook traffic. See attached: redwood_egress_ips.csv (this is our standard published range; we can pin a small subset per-deployment for strict allowlists).

3) Ports and protocols:
- For PrivateLink: allow HTTPS (443) to the interface endpoints we create; no inbound ports required from Redwood IPs.
- For VPC peering: allow outbound TCP/443 plus custom ports for metrics (TCP/9000) if you want our telemetry to push to your endpoints.

4) TLS model:
- We support both customer-terminated TLS (recommended for strict cert control) and Redwood-managed TLS. If you terminate at ALB and expect mTLS downstream, we’ll need the CA bundle and service account mapping.

5) IAM/service account:
- For peering we do not require cross-account IAM roles; for PrivateLink we will need a service consumer role to create/accept the endpoint (we can provide a CloudFormation snippet).

Next steps from infra perspective:
- Ava: if you can share the inventory we’ll produce a connection checklist with exact CIDR/routing examples within 24–48 hours.
- Tom: confirm whether you want an initial POC on peering (recommended) or to evaluate PrivateLink first. If peering, share the account IDs for peering config.

I’ll add a short network diagram and the CloudFormation snippet into the checklist.

Best —
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
